items.prompt: A broad permit precedes a restrictive deny. What is the concern?
options: The permit may shadow the deny
items.explanation: First-match processing can make later entries unreachable.

items.prompt: A switch receives source MAC A and destination MAC B on Fa0/3. Which entry can it learn directly from this arrival?
options: A belongs on Fa0/3 in the receiving VLAN
items.explanation: Learning uses the source address and incoming port. The destination lookup is a separate forwarding step.

items.prompt: An application works by IP but not by name. Which focused test is most useful next?
options: Inspect resolver settings and query the intended DNS record
items.explanation: The working IP connection narrows the investigation toward name resolution or name-dependent application behavior.

items.prompt: On a broadcast segment, two DROTHER neighbors are 2-WAY with each other. What is the best interpretation?
options: All 2-WAY states prove a broken link
This can be normal; inspect their DR/BDR adjacencies
items.explanation: Not all pairs on a broadcast network form FULL adjacencies. DROTHER routers form full adjacencies with the DR/BDR.

items.prompt: An unknown unicast arrives in VLAN 20. Where is it flooded?
items.explanation: Flooding remains inside the VLAN and obeys forwarding state.

items.prompt: 10.4.8.17 matches /8 and 10.4.8.0/24. Which prefix is used?
items.explanation: The /24 is more specific.

items.prompt: DAI blocks a legitimate statically addressed client. Which condition deserves inspection?
options: Whether the client needs an OSPF router ID
Whether all switch ports should become trusted immediately
Whether it has a valid binding or explicit validation policy
items.explanation: A static client may lack a DHCP-learned binding. Plan appropriate validation rather than broadly disabling protection.

items.prompt: An API returns HTTP 202 for a network change. Which conclusion is justified?
options: The request was accepted for processing; completion still needs checking
The change is verified on every device
items.explanation: 202 indicates acceptance, not necessarily completed processing or validated network behavior.

items.prompt: Which address is outside the RFC 1918 private ranges?
items.explanation: The private 172 range is 172.16.0.0 through 172.31.255.255. Similar decimal prefixes outside that interval are not private for that reason.

items.prompt: Give the network address for 172.16.102.119/27. Enter a dotted IPv4 address.
items.explanation: 172.16.102.119/27 belongs to 172.16.102.96/27; broadcast 172.16.102.127; 30 ordinary usable host addresses.

items.prompt: In {"enabled":true,"vlan":10}, what type is enabled?
items.explanation: Unquoted true is a JSON boolean. "true" would be a string and would not be the same value/type.

items.prompt: What does successful ICMP prove about HTTPS?
options: Only that this ICMP exchange succeeded
items.explanation: Service-specific testing is still required.

items.prompt: Installed routes: 10.0.0.0/8 via 192.0.2.202 (AD 1); 10.107.5.32/28 via 192.0.2.142 (AD 110); default via 192.0.2.71. Which next-hop IPv4 address is eligible for 10.107.5.37? Enter only the next-hop address.
items.explanation: The more specific matching installed prefix wins; a lower AD on the less specific route does not override it.

items.prompt: A gateway ping succeeds, but a website name does not resolve. Which test best narrows this new symptom?
options: Change the VLAN without checking it
items.explanation: Gateway reachability and name resolution test different functions. Inspect resolver settings and the DNS response.

items.prompt: Which action best describes shaping rather than policing?
options: Buffering traffic to smooth its transmission rate
items.explanation: Shaping uses queues to regulate output. Policing typically drops or remarks excess according to its policy.

items.prompt: Local VLAN 20 works but cross-switch VLAN 20 fails. Which evidence is directly useful?
items.explanation: The inter-switch VLAN path may be missing.

items.prompt: Why document unused ranges in a summary?
options: The summary can attract traffic to those ranges
items.explanation: A summary covers all addresses in its range.

items.prompt: A controller accepts a policy request while one target device is offline. What proves completion?
options: Device convergence and intended behavior, not acceptance alone
Only the number of API calls
items.explanation: Acceptance can precede execution. Check deployment status, actual state, and traffic behavior.

items.prompt: An 802.1Q trunk has different native VLANs on its ends. What needs correction?
options: The inconsistent interpretation of untagged traffic
items.explanation: Native VLAN consistency matters because untagged traffic is associated with the configured native VLAN.

items.prompt: Installed routes: 10.0.0.0/8 via 192.0.2.238 (AD 1); 10.74.5.128/28 via 192.0.2.40 (AD 110); default via 192.0.2.110. Which next-hop IPv4 address is eligible for 10.74.5.142? Enter only the next-hop address.
items.explanation: The more specific matching installed prefix wins; a lower AD on the less specific route does not override it.

items.prompt: An ACL has these entries in order: 10 permit ip host 192.168.127.11 any; 20 deny ip 192.168.127.0 0.0.0.255 any; 30 permit ip any any. What happens to a packet sourced by 192.168.127.11? Enter permit or deny.
items.explanation: ACLs stop at the first matching entry. Here the host permit matches first.

items.prompt: Which evidence tests a restriction most directly?
options: Both allowed and denied flows behave as expected
items.explanation: Positive and negative tests are needed.

items.prompt: Give the broadcast address for 172.31.19.9/20. Enter a dotted IPv4 address.
items.explanation: 172.31.19.9/20 belongs to 172.31.16.0/20; broadcast 172.31.31.255; 4094 ordinary usable host addresses.

items.prompt: Which pair distinguishes a Rapid STP role from a state?
options: Forwarding is a role; root is a state
Alternate is a role; discarding is a state
Both words identify IP routing metrics
items.explanation: Roles describe topology function, while states describe forwarding/learning behavior.

items.prompt: In an OSPF route’s [110/20] field, what does 20 normally represent?
items.explanation: The displayed pair is administrative distance followed by metric; OSPF uses cost as its metric.

items.prompt: The active gateway loses its upstream path but its LAN interface remains up. What design consideration matters?
options: Tracking relevant upstream health to influence gateway role
items.explanation: LAN-side liveness alone may not reflect remote reachability. Appropriate tracking can help align the active role with a usable path.

items.prompt: An ACL selects addresses for NAT. Does this by itself mean nonmatching traffic is denied on the interface?
options: Yes; every ACL definition filters every interface
Yes; NAT always replaces firewall policy
No; NAT selection and interface filtering are separate contexts
items.explanation: The meaning of a match depends on how the ACL is used. A NAT selector is not automatically an applied traffic filter.

items.prompt: For DHCP snooping, which path is the intended trust candidate in a basic access design?
items.explanation: Trust follows the legitimate server direction. Trusting all client ports defeats the purpose of rejecting rogue server messages.

items.prompt: Give the number of usable host addresses for 172.16.77.63/27. Enter digits only.
items.explanation: 172.16.77.63/27 belongs to 172.16.77.32/27; broadcast 172.16.77.63; 30 ordinary usable host addresses.

items.prompt: How should overlap be checked?
items.explanation: Two reservations may overlap even when their gateways differ.

items.prompt: Give the broadcast address for 172.25.197.15/26. Enter a dotted IPv4 address.
items.explanation: 172.25.197.15/26 belongs to 172.25.197.0/26; broadcast 172.25.197.63; 62 ordinary usable host addresses.

items.prompt: Give the number of usable host addresses for 172.30.133.72/25. Enter digits only.
items.explanation: 172.30.133.72/25 belongs to 172.30.133.0/25; broadcast 172.30.133.127; 126 ordinary usable host addresses.

items.prompt: Give the network address for 172.18.92.186/27. Enter a dotted IPv4 address.
items.explanation: 172.18.92.186/27 belongs to 172.18.92.160/27; broadcast 172.18.92.191; 30 ordinary usable host addresses.

items.prompt: For 192.168.12.70/26, which is an ordinary valid on-link gateway candidate?
items.explanation: The network is .64/26, with usable .65–.126. .1 is outside the subnet and .127 is its broadcast address.

items.prompt: A /24 client sends to a server outside its subnet. Its ARP request should normally ask for which address?
options: The DNS server regardless of destination
The remote server IP on every LAN
items.explanation: The Ethernet next hop for a remote destination is normally the on-link gateway. The IP packet still targets the remote server.

items.prompt: Which DNS record type provides an IPv6 address?
items.explanation: AAAA records contain IPv6 addresses; A records contain IPv4 addresses and CNAME supplies an alias.

items.prompt: Which proposed /26 network boundary is aligned within 192.168.1.0/24?
items.explanation: /26 blocks start at .0, .64, .128, and .192. An arbitrary host value cannot be used as the network boundary.

items.prompt: What is the final conventional usable host in 10.8.7.144/28?
items.explanation: The block spans .144–.159. Network and broadcast consume its endpoints, leaving .145–.158 for conventional hosts.

items.prompt: Two tenants reuse the same subnet but require independent routing tables on one device. Which mechanism fits?
items.explanation: A VRF creates a separate routing/forwarding context. Any communication between contexts needs an intentional design.

items.prompt: Which /28 network is aligned?
items.explanation: /28 blocks start at multiples of 16.

items.prompt: Which representation correctly compresses 2001:0db8:0010:0000:0000:0000:0000:0010?
items.explanation: Only one :: is permitted in an IPv6 address; it represents the required consecutive zero groups.

items.prompt: Which reservation overlaps 10.20.0.0/26?
items.explanation: The /26 reserves .0 through .63.

items.prompt: Why specify an exit interface with an IPv6 link-local static next hop?
options: The link identifies the scope of the next-hop address
Link-local addresses are globally unique server names
items.explanation: A link-local address is meaningful on a particular link and can be reused on other links.

items.prompt: A subnet must hold 50 endpoint addresses plus one gateway. What is the smallest conventional prefix that fits?
items.explanation: A /26 supplies 62 conventional usable addresses. /27 supplies only 30, too few for 51 required addresses.

items.prompt: What exactly summarizes adjacent 10.20.0.0/26 and 10.20.0.64/26?
items.explanation: The combined interval is .0 through .127, an aligned /25.

items.prompt: Give the number of usable host addresses for 172.24.139.22/25. Enter digits only.
items.explanation: 172.24.139.22/25 belongs to 172.24.139.0/25; broadcast 172.24.139.127; 126 ordinary usable host addresses.

items.prompt: Which address is outside the RFC 1918 private ranges?
items.explanation: The private 172 range is 172.16.0.0 through 172.31.255.255. Similar decimal prefixes outside that interval are not private for that reason.

items.prompt: Which evidence best verifies a repaired address plan?
options: Recorded host settings and local/remote tests
items.explanation: Configuration and observed reachability support the plan.

items.prompt: Which gateway is usable in 10.20.0.64/27?
items.explanation: The usable interval is .65 through .94.

items.prompt: How should overlap be checked?
items.explanation: Two reservations may overlap even when their gateways differ.

items.prompt: Where should the helper for a remote DHCP server normally be applied?
options: The router interface receiving the client broadcasts
items.explanation: Relay begins on the client-facing interface so it can forward the original client broadcast toward the server.

items.prompt: Why document unused ranges in a summary?
options: The summary can attract traffic to those ranges
items.explanation: A summary covers all addresses in its range.

items.prompt: Give the broadcast address for 172.28.200.6/25. Enter a dotted IPv4 address.
items.explanation: 172.28.200.6/25 belongs to 172.28.200.0/25; broadcast 172.28.200.127; 126 ordinary usable host addresses.

items.prompt: Give the network address for 172.26.47.99/28. Enter a dotted IPv4 address.
items.explanation: 172.26.47.99/28 belongs to 172.26.47.96/28; broadcast 172.26.47.111; 14 ordinary usable host addresses.
